findings.evidence: “If it prints anything, ask the user to commit or stash first, or work in a separate clean `git worktree` from HEAD” blocks migration even for unrelated untracked files or non-overlapping edits. The HEAD-based alternative also excludes uncommitted application changes that may be relevant to the requested upgrade.
findings.fix: Record the initial status and preserve existing edits by default. Check whether changes overlap the migration targets; request a checkpoint or an explicitly approved isolated worktree only when the codemod cannot safely operate without it. Do not require committing or stashing unrelated changes.

findings.evidence: The elementary Button and LibButton examples expand standard native-prop forwarding into two implementations, including “return <button ref={ref} data-variant={variant} {...rest} />;”. Their implementation mechanics add little beyond activating the React-major compatibility distinction.
findings.fix: Compress these two elementary wrappers into a short typed comparison of the React 19 ref prop and React 18-compatible forwardRef signature. Retain the generic List example and its explanation of inference erasure, which supply the non-obvious knowledge.

findings.evidence: Activation checklist, no explanation needed: native props via `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>`, variants as a discriminated union, `children: ReactNode`, an explicit state type when the initializer is `null`, `[]` or one member of a literal union.
findings.fix: Keep only the item models get wrong (an explicit state type when the initializer is `null`, `[]` or one literal member). Drop `children: ReactNode` and discriminated-union variants because current models already write them.

Also add one should-trigger query that never names React or TypeScript, for example 'my table's date column formatter crashes at runtime with toLocaleDateString is not a function'.

Show the separate-file setup explicitly. Export `columnsFor` (or `col`) from the app module and start the type-test file with `import { columnsFor } from './columns'; type User = ...; const col = columnsFor<User>();`. As written, `col` is not exported, so a separate `columns.type-test.tsx` fails with 'Cannot find name col'. That error satisfies the @ts-expect-error directive, so the test passes vacuously.
